Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Winter light therapy reduced depression scores in adolescents.
Sentence: "Winter light therapy increases vitamin D (Δ = 8.2 ng/mL, p < 0.001) and reduces depression (ΔPHQ-9=-3.1, p = 0.005)."
Measured as: depression (PHQ-9)
Population: Chinese adolescents in winter RCTs (N = 200)
Intervention: Winter light therapy
Comparator: Not reported
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 7,321
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Consuming UV-exposed mushrooms did not improve depression outcomes compared with control; no between-group differences in brain health indices.
Sentence: "Consuming UV light-exposed mushrooms did not improve brain health outcomes."
Measured as: depression (BDI-II, PHQ-9)
Population: Adults without severe depression, cardiovascular disease, or Type 2 Diabetes, age 43 ± 11 y, BMI 29.8 kg/m2
Intervention: Two daily servings (168 g/d) of UV-exposed cremini mushrooms providing ~800 IU/d vitamin D2 for 6 weeks
Comparator: 2 tsp/d breadcrumbs (control)
Design: non-randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 41
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
